post-full-title: Saxophone sheet music maker: write and share your scores

post-content: Saxophone parts are transposing parts, and the alto, tenor, soprano, and baritone each sit in a different key. A saxophone sheet music maker handles the transposition, the range, and the playback so you write the part the player reads.  runs in your browser with each saxophone preconfigured to its concert-pitch offset. This article walks through writing your first saxophone score, the sax-specific features that matter, and how to share or export what you've written.
post-content 3: Writing your first saxophone score in Flat
post-content 4: Open Flat, sign in, and start a new score. Pick the saxophone you're writing for from the instrument list: Alto Sax (in Eb), Tenor Sax (in Bb), Soprano Sax (in Bb), or Baritone Sax (in Eb). Flat sets up a treble-clef staff with the right transposition built in. Click any rest and either type the note name or click the staff position. The  covers the basics if you want a fuller walkthrough.
post-content 7: A saxophone part isn't just notes in treble clef. Here's what Flat gives you for the things saxophonists actually need to write:
post-content 8: Pick Alto, Tenor, Soprano, or Baritone Sax and Flat applies the right transposition. Switch the instrument later and Flat re-transposes the existing notes so the line still sounds the same.💡
post-content 11: Sax phrasing depends on slurs that tell the player which notes to take in one breath. Select the first note, press S, and Flat draws the slur. The playback respects it.💡
post-content 14: Accent, marcato, staccato, tenuto, and detached legato cover the everyday tonguing markings. For jazz parts, you'll reach for accents and ghost-note noteheads constantly.💡
post-content 15: Articulations for jazz and classical phrasing.
post-content 17: If you're writing a lead sheet or a sax-and-rhythm-section chart, chord symbols (Cmaj7, F♯m, Bb7) sit above the staff and follow your style preferences. Useful for any jazz, funk, or pop sax part.💡
post-content 20: Hairpins and dynamic letters are on the dynamics toolbar, and the playback engine shapes the volume along the hairpin. A long crescendo into a forte sounds like one in your preview.💡
post-content 21: Crescendos and dynamics that play back.
post-content 23: Sax parts in jazz and pop almost always loop a section with a fill or a tag. Flat supports repeat barlines, first/second endings, and multi-pass repeats so you don't write the same chorus twice.💡
post-content 26: Sharing and exporting your saxophone score
post-content 27: When the score is ready, click Share for a public link, invite collaborators by email for real-time editing, or open the  to download as PDF, MIDI, or MusicXML. PDF is what most sax players want on a stand, already in their transposition. MIDI sends the line into a DAW. MusicXML lets another notation tool open the file with the transposition and chord symbols intact. A bandleader can hand each section a transposed part from the same source score.
post-content 29: Find inspiration in the Flat community
post-content 30: Flat hosts more than 100,000 user-published scores, including a lot of sax solos, lead sheets, and big-band charts.  to see how other composers voiced a section, paced a solo, or laid out a chart. You can clone any public score into your own account and start editing from there.
post-content 33: Most sax notation tools require an install and a learning curve before you write a single note. Flat opens in your browser, the Eb or Bb transposition is set the moment you pick the instrument, and the playback uses recorded saxophone samples instead of a generic reed sound. Real-time collaboration lets a teacher, bandleader, or arranger work in the same score with you without sending files back and forth.

mcp-faq 2: How do I write saxophone sheet music online for free?
mcp-faq 3: Sign up for a free Flat account, create a new score, pick the saxophone you're writing for, and start entering notes. The free tier covers personal use including PDF export and public sharing.
mcp-faq 4: Does Flat transpose for alto and tenor sax automatically?
mcp-faq 5: Yes. Alto and Baritone Sax are in Eb, Tenor and Soprano Sax are in Bb. Flat applies the right transposition the moment you pick the instrument, and switching instruments mid-project re-transposes the notes.
mcp-faq 6: Can I write a jazz lead sheet with chord symbols for sax?
mcp-faq 7: Yes. Chord symbols sit above the staff and follow your style preferences (m vs −, maj vs △). Useful for any sax part that needs a rhythm-section backing.
mcp-faq 8: Can I export a transposed saxophone part to PDF?
mcp-faq 9: Yes. Open the score, click Export, and choose PDF. The export uses whichever transposition view you have set, so each section gets a part they can read directly.
mcp-faq 10: Can I collaborate on a sax score in real time?
mcp-faq 11: Yes. Share the score with other Flat users and you can all edit and view it at the same time. Useful for bandleaders, arrangers, and teachers working with players remotely.
